Aerial Wildlife Survey Report  
Wildlife Management Unit 501 Aerial Ungulate Survey (2018-19) 
 
Background 
Cold Lake Wildlife Management Unit (WMU 501) covers an area of 2,132 km2 and is located southwest of Cold 
Lake. The WMU is bordered by Saskatchewan to the east. Agriculture is predominant throughout much of the unit, 
covering 33% of the landscape; however, several tracts of broadleaf (22%), coniferous (3%), and mixed-wood 
(1%) stands occur north of Highway 55, along the Saskatchewan border, and in the southeastern portion of the 
WMU. Riparian areas occur along the Beaver River and provide key summer and winter ungulate habitat. 
Substantial water bodies within WMU 501 include Cold and Muriel lakes. Urban centres include Bonnyville and 
Cold Lake, as well as several small communities and summer villages, which are dispersed throughout the unit. Oil 
and gas extraction activities are common, with abundant oilfield and related traffic through much of the area. The 
Cold Lake First Nation and Kehewin Cree Nation reside within WMU 501. 
 
The objective of the 2018/19 survey was to assess the status of the ungulate (moose, white-tailed deer, mule deer) 
population in WMU 501 by estimating abundance, density and the age-sex composition. 
 
Survey Method 
An aerial survey for ungulates was conducted December 11 to 13, 2018 using distance sampling techniques 
(Buckland et al., 2001; Thomas et al., 2010). A total of 177 north-south transect lines (survey effort = 1,271.2 
kilometres) were flown with two jet ranger helicopters, each outfitted with rear bubble windows to maximize 
visibility. Ungulates were classified by age class (adult or juvenile) and sex. Other wildlife sightings were recorded. 
 
Results 
Moose 
A total of 130 moose were observed in 73 groups, which included 69 cows, 44 calves, and 17 bulls (3 antlerless 
and 14 with antlers). The estimated density was 0.229 moose/km2 (90% CI 0.176 – 0.298) and the estimated 
abundance was 415 individuals (90% CI 319 – 540; Table 1). A total of 130 moose were successfully classified 
and the bull:cow:calf ratio was estimated to be 25:100:64. 
 
White-tailed Deer 
A total of 1,097 white-tailed deer were observed in 421 groups, which included 495 does, 341 fawns, 145 bucks, 
and 116 unclassified individuals. The estimated density was 2.405 deer/km2 (90% CI 2.097 – 2.759) and the 
estimated abundance was 4,353 individuals (90% CI 3,795 – 4,992; Table 1). A total of 981 white-tailed deer were 
successfully classified and the buck:doe:fawn ratio was estimated to be 29:100:69. 
 
Mule Deer 
A total of 66 mule deer were observed in 13 groups, which included 36 does, 23 fawns, 6 bucks, and 1 unclassified 
individual. A total of 65 mule deer were successfully classified and the buck:doe:fawn ratio was estimated to be 
17:100:64. Given low sample size, density and abundance estimates were not calculated for mule deer.
